editorial.marketOverview: Thursday's broad selloff remains the latest observed cash-market backdrop. Nasdaq -2.25%, S&P 500 -2.02%, and over 90% S&P decliners accompany elevated volatility. New November 19 evening technical commentary describes Nasdaq-100 and SOX below uptrend lines, NYSE downside volume 87%, and VIX at its highest close since March; these corroborate existing weakness rather than create a new catalyst.
editorial.whatChanged: Relative to the 20:12 EST assessment, an 18:33 EST technical commentary added broken Nasdaq-100/SOX trend lines and 87% NYSE downside volume. This increases corroboration of the established bearish picture but does not change the directional three-session path. Open Watch was refreshed at 2026-11-20T01:24:04+00:00 with 171 curated events; no independently established new path-changing catalyst.
editorial.marketInterpretation: Weak breadth, semiconductor trend deterioration and volatility expansion remain consistent with distribution. The latest technical commentary is secondary evidence and cannot substitute for synchronized official prices. A rebound after heavy selling remains possible, but durable recovery requires stronger relative performance and broader participation. Prior curve and oil observations are stale or maturity-mismatched.
editorial.threeDayPath: Friday November 20 is the immediate test: a relief rebound that fails in QQQ and SOX would support continued weakness Monday November 23 and Tuesday November 24. Michigan final sentiment at 10:00 EST and inflation expectations are future catalysts, not observed market reactions. A broad, sustained semiconductor-led recovery would challenge the bearish path.
editorial.bullCase: A sharp oversold bounce is plausible after broad selling. Require sustained QQQ versus SPY outperformance, SOX/SMH leadership, improving breadth and declining volatility with stable yields before upgrading the outlook. Anthropic's prior IPO premium is company-specific, not sufficient market confirmation.
editorial.bearCase: Nasdaq -2.25%, broad S&P selling, elevated VIX and fresh analyst-observed breaks in NDX/SOX uptrends favor further downside if Friday's bounce fails. NYSE downside volume of 87% adds confirmation but is sourced from technical commentary rather than an independent exchange feed.
